topic: Prompt of the week: the "what should I double-check?" prompt (after AI voter guides got facts wrong)
post:
AI answers sound confident even when they're wrong.
This prompt makes the AI tell you what to double-check. 🔍

Why this week:
The Washington Post and NPR found AI chatbots giving wrong election info, from made-up races to wrong registration deadlines.

The lesson: the risky part isn't using AI. It's not knowing which parts to verify. ⚠️

Prompt of the week 👇
Add this to the end of any important question:

"After your answer, list every fact in it that I should verify before acting: dates, numbers, names, rules and deadlines. For each one, tell me what kind of official source would confirm it, and mark how confident you are: high, medium or low."

What you get:
✅ Your answer
✅ A checklist of the risky bits
✅ Where to check each one

It won't make the AI right. It makes it easier for YOU to catch it when it's wrong.

Why it matters:
Anything local, recent or high-stakes is where AI is most likely to slip. A 30-second check beats a costly mistake. 💡

Practical takeaway:
Save this prompt as a text shortcut, so it's one keystroke away. ⌨️

What's one thing you always double-check? 👇
